messages.content:
Offline agentic trajectory source.
Title: task_[mms_issue]airplane_mode_on|bad_network_preference|bad_wifi_calling|break_apn_mms_setting|break_app_both_permissions|data_mode_off|data_usage_exceeded|unseat_sim_card|user_abroad_roaming_disabled_off[PERSONA:Hard].txt
Treat this content as one complete trajectory/workflow context.
Trajectory content:
AGENT: Hi! How can I help you today?
USER: Oh hello. I'm having a bit of trouble with my phone. I've been trying to send a picture message to my daughter - a photo of my grandchildren - but it just won't go through. It's been like this for a few hours now. Can you help me?
AGENT: I can help with that. First, I need to verify your account. Could you please provide your phone number?

Also, to troubleshoot the picture message issue, I'll need you to check a few things on your phone. Let's start by identifying you.
USER: Oh, of course. My phone number is 555-123-2002. My name is John Smith.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_customer_by_phone", "arguments": {"phone_number": "555-123-2002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}
AGENT: Thanks, John — I've found your account. Now let's troubleshoot the picture message issue.

Could you please run a diagnostic on your phone and tell me:

1. What does your status bar show (signal strength, network type, etc.)?
2. Can you check your network status?

If you have a tool to check whether you can send MMS, please run that as well and share the result.
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: ON
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Okay, I ran those checks. Here's what I got, though I'm not sure what it all means:

1. My status bar shows a little airplane icon and the battery at 80%.
2. The network check says Airplane Mode is ON, the SIM card status is "missing," cellular connection says "no service," mobile data is disabled, data roaming is disabled, and Wi-Fi is off.
3. And it says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Does any of that help figure out what's wrong?
AGENT: Yes, that helps a lot. The airplane icon and "Airplane Mode ON" are the main problem — when airplane mode is on, your phone can't connect to the cellular network at all, so calls, texts, and picture messages won't work.

Could you please turn **Airplane Mode OFF** on your phone, then check the status bar and network status again and let me know what it shows?
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: Okay, I turned Airplane Mode off. But... it still doesn't look right. Now the status bar shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" along with the 80% battery.

And the network check says Airplane Mode is OFF now, but the SIM card status is still "missing," cellular connection is "no service," no signal, mobile data is disabled, data roaming is disabled, and Wi-Fi is off.

I'm getting a little worried here - is something wrong with my phone?
AGENT: No need to worry — this looks like a SIM card issue, which is usually fixable.

The SIM status shows "missing," which means your phone isn't detecting the SIM card properly. Could you please **reseat the SIM card** on your phone — take it out and put it back in firmly?

After that, check the status bar and network status again and let me know what it shows.
TOOL_RESULT: SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: poor
Cellular Network Type: 2G
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: Progress! I took the SIM card out and put it back in. Here's what I see now:

The status bar shows a weak signal, "2G", and "Data Disabled", plus the 80% battery.

The network check now says the SIM card is "active", cellular connection is "connected", but the signal is poor, the network type is 2G, mobile data is still disabled, data roaming is disabled, and Wi-Fi is off.

So the SIM card seems okay now, but it's still not working. What should I try next?
AGENT: Good progress — the SIM is working now. There are two remaining issues to fix before picture messages will work:

1. **Network type is 2G.** MMS needs at least 3G, so we need to change that. Please use the option to set your network mode preference to **"4g_5g_preferred"** (or "4g_only").

2. **Mobile data is disabled.** Please turn **mobile data ON** as well.

Go ahead and do both, then check the status bar and network status again and let me know what you see.
USER: Oh dear, that's two things at once and I get a bit flustered with these settings. Could you walk me through them one at a time, please? Which one should I do first?
AGENT: No problem, let's take it one at a time.

**First:** change your network mode preference to **"4g_5g_preferred"**.

Go ahead and do that, then check the network status and tell me what the network type shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: That worked nicely! The network type now shows 5G, and the signal is excellent. Here's the full network status:

Airplane Mode OFF, SIM active, connected, signal excellent, network type 5G, but mobile data is still disabled, data roaming disabled, and Wi-Fi off.

What's next?
AGENT: Great — 5G with excellent signal now.

**Next:** turn **mobile data ON**.

Once that's done, check the status bar and network status again, and let me know what you see.
TOOL_RESULT: Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: Mobile data is now ON. Here's what I see:

Status bar: excellent signal, 5G, "Data Enabled", 80% battery.

Network status: Airplane Mode OFF, SIM active, connected, excellent signal, 5G, mobile data enabled, but data roaming is still disabled and Wi-Fi is off.

Should I try sending the picture message now?
AGENT: Yes, please try sending the picture message now and let me know if it goes through.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Hmm, it still says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages. That's frustrating - I thought we were getting somewhere.

Is there something else that could be blocking it?
AGENT: We're close — let's check a few more things that can block MMS.

Could you please check the following on your phone and share the results:

1. **APN settings** — specifically whether the MMSC URL is set.
2. **Wi-Fi Calling status** — whether it's ON or OFF.
3. **Messaging app permissions** — whether "storage" and "sms" permissions are granted.
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
TOOL_RESULT: The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
TOOL_RESULT: App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.
USER: Okay, here's what I found:

1. **APN settings:** The APN name is "internet", but the MMSC URL — the thing for picture messages — says "Not Set". That doesn't sound good.
2. **Wi-Fi Calling:** It's currently ON.
3. **Messaging app permissions:** It only has permission for "phone". It doesn't have "storage" or "sms".

So there are a few problems, it seems. What should I fix first?
AGENT: Good catches — all three need fixing, and they're each contributing to the problem.

**First:** let's fix the APN settings. Please **reset the APN settings** on your phone.

After resetting, you'll need to **reboot your device** for the changes to apply. Go ahead and do the reset now, then tell me when you're ready for the reboot step.
TOOL_RESULT: APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: I've done the APN reset. It says the APN settings will reset when I reboot.

I'm a little nervous about rebooting though — will I lose any of my photos or anything on my phone?
AGENT: No, you won't lose anything — rebooting is just restarting your phone, like turning it off and back on. Your photos, contacts, and settings all stay exactly as they are. It's a completely safe step.

Please go ahead and reboot your device now, then let me know when it's back up.
TOOL_RESULT: Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
USER: Okay, the phone restarted and it's back up. The status bar looks fine — excellent signal, 5G, data enabled.

And good news on the APN: the MMSC URL is now set to "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc". So that part looks fixed.

What's next?
AGENT: The MMSC is set — that's a big one fixed.

**Next:** Wi-Fi Calling is ON, which can interfere with MMS. Please **turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF**.

Once that's done, let me know and we'll finish with the app permissions.
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Done — Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.

What's next for the app permissions?
AGENT: **Last step:** the messaging app is missing two permissions it needs. Please grant the messaging app both:

1. **storage** permission
2. **sms** permission

Once both are granted, let me know and then try sending the picture message again.
TOOL_RESULT: Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Well, I granted both permissions, but I tried again and it *still* says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages. 

I have to say, I'm getting a bit discouraged here — we've changed so many things and it still won't work. 

Oh, one thing I should mention — I'm currently abroad in France visiting my daughter. Could that have something to do with it?
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1001"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "enable_roaming", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1001"}}
TOOL_RESULT: Roaming enabled successfully
AGENT: Done — I've enabled data roaming on your line at no charge.

Now, on your phone, please **turn on data roaming** as well (your network check showed it was disabled). Once that's on, try sending the picture message again and let me know if it goes through.
TOOL_RESULT: Data Roaming is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Data roaming is now ON. But I tried sending the picture message again, and it *still* says it cannot send MMS. 

I'm sorry, I feel like we're going in circles. Is there anything else that could be causing this?
AGENT: No need to apologize — we've worked through the usual causes, so let's re-verify everything at once to see what's still off after all those changes.

Could you please run your checks again and share:

1. **Status bar** — what icons show now
2. **Network status** — signal, network type, mobile data, roaming, Wi-Fi
3. **APN settings** — is the MMSC URL still set?
4. **Wi-Fi Calling status** — ON or OFF
5. **Messaging app permissions** — are "storage" and "sms" granted?
6. **MMS check** — can it send now?
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: Yes
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
TOOL_RESULT: App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, storage, phone.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Okay, I ran everything again. Here's the full picture:

1. **Status bar:** excellent signal, 5G, "Data Enabled", 80% battery.
2. **Network status:** Airplane Mode OFF, SIM active, connected, excellent signal, 5G, mobile data ON, data roaming ON, Wi-Fi off.
3. **APN settings:** APN is "internet", and the MMSC URL is still set to "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc".
4. **Wi-Fi Calling:** OFF.
5. **Messaging app permissions:** it now has "sms", "storage", and "phone".
6. **MMS check:** still says it cannot send MMS.

Everything looks like it should be right now, but it still won't send. I really hope we can figure this out.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_data_usage", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1001"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1001", "data_used_gb": "3.2", "data_limit_gb": "5.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}

With Airplane Mode now off, "No Signal" means your phone isn't picking up the cellular network. Let's check your SIM card:

1. **Reset APN settings** — this will restore the correct MMSC URL. After doing it, you must **reboot your device** for the change to apply.
2. **Turn OFF Wi-Fi Calling** (Settings → Network & Internet → Calls & SMS → Wi-Fi Calling → OFF).
3. **Grant the messaging app permissions:**
   - Grant **storage** permission

Go ahead and do these, then try sending a picture message again and let me know the result.
USER: Oh my, that's a lot at once — I'm worried I'll get confused and mess something up. Could you please walk me through these one at a time? Let's start with the first one.

**Step 1: Reset your APN settings.**

Once you've done that, tell me when it's complete and we'll move on. (Note: after the reset, we'll need to reboot your phone for it to take effect — but let's do that as its own step.)

USER: Hi there! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages on my phone. It's been happening for the past few hours and I can't seem to send any pictures. Can you help me fix this?
AGENT: I can help with that. First, I need to identify you. Could you please provide your phone number?
USER: Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002.

Which phone number/line is affected? You have a few lines on your account. Also, could you check your device's status bar for me — I'll walk you through the diagnostics.
USER: The affected line is 555-123-2002. Let me check my status bar for you.
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I checked my status bar. It shows that Airplane Mode is turned on, and my battery is at 80%.
AGENT: Thanks. Airplane Mode being on would block all cellular service, which MMS needs. Let's start there.

Please turn **Airplane Mode OFF**, then check your status bar again and tell me what you see (signal strength, network type, and mobile data status).

Also, to confirm — which line are you trying to send MMS from?
USER: I'm trying to send MMS from the 555-123-2002 line. Let me turn off Airplane Mode now.
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I've turned Airplane Mode off. Now my status bar shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled", with the battery still at 80%.
AGENT: Thanks. Two issues there: no signal, and mobile data is disabled. MMS needs both cellular service and mobile data.

First, let's check the network connection more thoroughly. Please run `check_network_status` on your device and share the results with me.

Also, please turn **mobile data ON** and let me know if the "Data Disabled" indicator changes.
USER: I can only handle one action at a time — could you please tell me which one you'd like me to do first?
AGENT: No problem — let's do one at a time.

First, please run `check_network_status` on your device and share the results with me.

Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none

- Airplane Mode: OFF
- SIM Card Status: **missing**
- Cellular Connection: no service
- Cellular Signal: none
- Cellular Network Type: none
- Mobile Data Enabled: No
- Data Roaming Enabled: No
- Wi-Fi Radio: OFF / Not connected

It looks like my SIM card is showing as missing. That might explain the no signal issue.
AGENT: That's exactly it — the SIM card is showing as missing, which is why you have no service. Let's fix that.

Please run `reseat_sim_card()` on your device to ensure the SIM card is correctly inserted, then check the status again and let me know what it shows.
TOOL_RESULT: SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Done — I re-seated the SIM card. Now my status bar shows a poor signal on 2G, and data is still disabled. Battery at 80%.
AGENT: Good progress — the SIM is being detected now. But two things still need fixing:

1. You're on **2G**, which isn't suitable for MMS (it needs at least 3G).
2. **Mobile data is still disabled**.

Let's handle the network mode first. Please run `set_network_mode_preference(mode="4g_5g_preferred")` on your device to switch to a network mode that includes 3G/4G/5G, then let me know the result.
TOOL_RESULT: Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: That worked well — now my status bar shows an excellent signal on 5G. But data is still disabled. Battery's at 80%.
AGENT: Excellent — 5G with a strong signal. Now let's enable mobile data, since MMS requires it.

Please turn **mobile data ON**, then check your status bar and let me know what it shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Mobile data is now ON. My status bar now shows: excellent signal on 5G, data enabled, battery at 80%. 

Should I try sending an MMS now?

MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set

- Current APN Name: internet
- MMSC URL (for picture messages): **Not Set**

So the MMSC URL is missing — that's probably why MMS isn't working. What should I do?
AGENT: That's the culprit. The MMSC URL is missing, and it's required for MMS.

Please run `reset_apn_settings()` to reset your APN settings, then let me know once that's done.
TOOL_RESULT: APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, it says the APN settings will reset at reboot. So it seems I'll need to restart my phone for that to take effect. Should I go ahead and reboot?
AGENT: Yes, please go ahead and reboot your device with `reboot_device()` so the APN changes apply. Let me know once it's back up and what your status bar shows.

Restarting network services...

Title: task_[mms_issue]airplane_mode_on|bad_network_preference|bad_wifi_calling|break_apn_mms_setting|break_app_storage_permission|data_mode_off|data_usage_exceeded|unseat_sim_card|user_abroad_roaming_disabled_off[PERSONA:Easy].txt
Treat this content as one complete trajectory/workflow context.
Trajectory content:
AGENT: Hi! How can I help you today?
USER: Hi there! I'm having some trouble with my phone. I've been trying to send MMS messages for the past few hours, but they just won't go through. I'm currently traveling in France, and I'm not sure what's going on. Can you help me figure this out?
AGENT: I can help with that. First, I need to identify you. Could you please provide your phone number, or your full name and date of birth?
USER: Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_customer_by_phone", "arguments": {"phone_number": "555-123-2002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}
AGENT: Thanks, John — I've found your account. You mentioned you're traveling in France and having trouble sending MMS.

Since MMS needs data connectivity, let me check a couple of things. First, which of your lines are you using while traveling? Also, can you check your phone's status bar for me — what icons do you see at the top of the screen?
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
USER: I'm just using my usual line — I only have the one number.

As for the status bar, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. That's it — I don't see any signal bars or anything else. Does that airplane icon mean anything?
AGENT: Yes — that airplane icon means **Airplane Mode is turned on**, which disables all cellular connectivity. That's almost certainly why your MMS messages won't send: with Airplane Mode on, your phone has no cellular service at all.

Could you please turn **Airplane Mode off**, then check the status bar again and let me know what you see?
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I've turned Airplane Mode off. Now the status bar shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," and the battery is still at 80%. Hmm, still no signal though. What should I do next?
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1001"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1002", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1002", "device_id": "D1002", "data_used_gb": 15.1, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-12-15", "last_sim_replacement_date": "2025-01-20", "suspension_start_date": null}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1003"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1003", "phone_number": "555-123-2003", "status": "Suspended", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1003", "data_used_gb": 0.0, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-06-30", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-10-05", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": "2025-02-01"}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "enable_roaming", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: Roaming enabled successfully
AGENT: I've enabled roaming on your line at no cost. 

Now, a couple of things to get service and MMS working:

1. **Reboot your device** — this helps the phone pick up the network.
2. Make sure **mobile data is turned on** (your status bar showed "Data Disabled," and MMS needs data).

After rebooting, please check the status bar again and let me know what you see — signal bars, network type (4G/5G), and whether data is enabled.
USER: That sounds good, thanks for enabling roaming. But you've given me two things to do at once — reboot the phone and turn on mobile data. I can only do one at a time, so could you tell me which one to start with?
AGENT: Sorry about that — let's do one at a time.

Please **turn on mobile data** first, then check the status bar and tell me what you see.
TOOL_RESULT: Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I turned on mobile data. But the status bar still shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" — it doesn't seem to have changed. Battery is still 80%. That's strange, isn't it?
AGENT: That is odd — thanks for checking. The status bar can be slow to refresh, so let's go ahead with the next step.

Please **reboot your device** now, then check the status bar again and let me know what you see.
TOOL_RESULT: Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Alright, I've rebooted the phone. But I have to say, I'm getting a little frustrated — the status bar still shows "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," same as before. Nothing seems to be working. What now?
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "D1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"device_id": "D1002", "device_type": "phone", "model": "Smartphone Pro Max", "imei": "234567890123456", "is_esim_capable": true, "activated": true, "activation_date": "2025-02-15 11:45:00", "last_esim_transfer_date": "2025-01-20 09:30:00"}
AGENT: Thanks for your patience. Let me have you check a few things on your phone directly.

Could you please check your **network status** (via your phone's settings/diagnostics) — I'd like to know:
- Is Airplane Mode off? (it should be now)
- What does the SIM card status show — is it **Missing**, **Locked**, or something else?

Also, could you check your **APN settings** — specifically whether they show as correct or incorrect?
USER: You've listed a few things there — check network status, check the SIM card status, and check the APN settings. I can only manage one at a time, so could you tell me which one you'd like me to start with?
AGENT: Let's start with **network status**. Please check it and tell me what it shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: Okay, here's what the network status shows:

- Airplane Mode: OFF
- SIM Card Status: **missing**
- Cellular Connection: no service
- Cellular Signal: none
- Network Type: none
- Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
- Data Roaming Enabled: **No**
- Wi-Fi: OFF and not connected

The SIM card status says "missing" — that seems important. Also, data roaming shows as disabled, even though you mentioned you enabled it on my line.
AGENT: Good catch — two things there.

The SIM showing as **missing** is the immediate problem: if the phone doesn't detect the SIM card, it can't connect to any network. Let's fix that first.

Please **reseat your SIM card** (remove it and put it back in firmly), then check the SIM status again and let me know what it shows.

As for the roaming setting — that's a device-side setting separate from the line setting I enabled. We'll tackle that after the SIM is detected.
TOOL_RESULT: SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Your SIM card is active and working.
USER: Good news — reseating the SIM card seems to have helped! The SIM status now shows it's **active and working**.

The status bar has changed too: I now see a weak signal (one bar), it says **2G**, and data is enabled. So I do have some signal now, though it's pretty weak. What's next?
AGENT: Progress! You now have service, but two issues remain for MMS:

1. **Network type is 2G** — MMS requires at least 3G. 2G isn't suitable.
2. **Data roaming is disabled on the device** — since you're in France, you need it on.

Let's fix the network type first. Please change your **network mode preference** to something that includes 4G/5G (e.g., "4G/5G preferred" or "4G only"), then tell me what the status bar shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: That worked nicely! I've set the network mode to 4G/5G preferred, and now the status bar shows:

- Signal: excellent (4 bars)
- Network: **5G**
- Data: enabled
- Battery: 80%

Much better than the 2G I had before! What's next?
AGENT: Excellent — 5G with strong signal. Now let's handle the device-side roaming.

Please **turn on data roaming** in your phone's settings, then tell me what the status bar shows and whether roaming is now enabled.
TOOL_RESULT: Data Roaming is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Done — data roaming is now **ON**. The status bar shows:

- Signal: excellent (4 bars)
- Network: **5G**
- Data: enabled
- Battery: 80%

So roaming is enabled on the device now. Should I try sending an MMS to see if it works?
AGENT: Yes, please go ahead and try sending an MMS now — let me know if it goes through.

If it still doesn't work, we'll check your APN settings next.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Hmm, no luck — I tried sending an MMS but it still **couldn't go through**. So we're not there yet. Should we check the APN settings now?
AGENT: Yes — let's check the APN settings. Please look at your **APN settings** and tell me what they show, especially whether the **MMSC URL** is set.
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
USER: Here's what the APN settings show:

- Current APN Name: **internet**
- MMSC URL (for picture messages): **Not Set**

So the MMSC URL is missing — that looks like it could be the problem. What should I do to fix it?
AGENT: That's the problem — a missing MMSC URL stops MMS from working. Let's reset the APN settings to restore it.

Please **reset your APN settings**, then **reboot your device**, and tell me what the APN settings show afterward.
USER: You've given me two steps there — reset the APN settings and then reboot. I can only do one at a time, so could you tell me which one to start with?
AGENT: Right — one at a time.

Please **reset your APN settings** first, then tell me what they show.
TOOL_RESULT: APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I reset the APN settings. It says "APN settings will reset at reboot" — so it looks like I need to restart the phone for it to take effect. Should I go ahead and reboot now?
AGENT: Yes, please **reboot your device** now, then check the APN settings and tell me what the MMSC URL shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
USER: The reboot is done, and now the APN settings show:

- Current APN Name: **internet**
- MMSC URL: **http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc** — it's set now!

So the MMSC URL is restored. Should I try sending an MMS again?
AGENT: Yes — please try sending an MMS again and let me know if it goes through.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Ugh, still no luck — I tried again and the MMS **still won't send**. That's frustrating, we've done quite a bit already. What else could be causing this?
AGENT: I know this is taking a while — we're getting close. Let me check one more thing that commonly affects MMS.

Could you check your **Wi-Fi Calling status** and tell me what it shows (ON or OFF)?
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
USER: It shows that **Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON**. Is that a problem for MMS?
AGENT: Yes — Wi-Fi Calling can conflict with MMS. Please **turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF**, then try sending an MMS again and let me know if it goes through.
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Okay, I turned Wi-Fi Calling off, and then tried sending an MMS — but it **still won't send**. So that wasn't it either. I'm really running out of ideas here — is there anything else we can try?
AGENT: One more common cause: the messaging app may lack the permissions it needs. Could you check the **messaging app's permissions** and tell me whether **storage** and **SMS** are listed as granted?
TOOL_RESULT: The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
TOOL_RESULT: App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.
USER: Here's what I found for the messaging app's permissions:

- **SMS**: granted
- **Phone**: granted
- **Storage**: **not** granted — it's not listed

So SMS is granted, but storage is missing. Does that matter for MMS?
AGENT: Yes — the messaging app needs **storage** permission to attach and handle MMS media. Let's grant it.

Please **grant storage permission to the messaging app**, then try sending an MMS again and let me know if it goes through.
TOOL_RESULT: Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: I granted the storage permission, but when I tried sending an MMS again, it **still won't go through**. 

We've tried quite a few things now. Is there anything else that could be blocking it?
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "transfer_to_human_agents", "arguments": {"summary": "Customer John Smith (C1001), traveling in France, cannot send MMS on line L1002 (555-123-2002). Troubleshooting completed: Airplane Mode turned off; SIM reseated (was showing missing); network mode set to 4G/5G (now 5G, excellent signal); roaming enabled on line and device; APN reset so MMSC URL restored; Wi-Fi Calling turned off; messaging app storage permission granted. MMS still fails to send. Requires further investigation."}}
TOOL_RESULT: Transfer successful
AGENT: YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
USER: ###TRANSFER###

USER: Here’s what I see now:

Same as before. So the MMSC URL looks like it’s set. What should we try next?

Roaming enabled (was off). MMS still fails; can_send_mms() reports cannot send. Needs further technical escalation."}}

USER: ###TRANSFER###

Offline agentic trajectory source.
Title: task_[mms_issue]airplane_mode_on|bad_network_preference|break_apn_mms_setting|break_app_both_permissions|data_mode_off|data_usage_exceeded|user_abroad_roaming_enabled_off[PERSONA:None].txt
Treat this content as one complete trajectory/workflow context.
Trajectory content:
AGENT: Hi! How can I help you today?
USER: Hi, I'm having trouble sending MMS messages using my messaging app. It's been happening for the past few hours and I'd really like to get it fixed.
AGENT: I can help with that. First, I need to identify you as a customer. Could you please provide your phone number?
USER: Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_customer_by_phone", "arguments": {"phone_number": "555-123-2002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}
AGENT: Thanks, John. I've found your account.

Let's troubleshoot your MMS issue. Could you first check your phone's status bar and tell me what it shows? Specifically I'd like to know about your signal strength, mobile data, and network type.
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
USER: Hmm, my status bar shows an airplane icon, so it looks like Airplane Mode is turned on. Battery is at 80%. I don't see any signal or mobile data icons.
AGENT: Thanks for checking. Airplane Mode being on would explain why you can't send MMS — it disables all cellular connectivity.

Could you please turn Airplane Mode off on your phone, then check the status bar again and let me know what you see?
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I've turned Airplane Mode off. Now the status bar shows a poor signal with what looks like 2G, and it says data is disabled. Battery still at 80%.
AGENT: Thanks. Two issues here:

1. **Mobile data is disabled** — please turn mobile data ON. MMS requires mobile data.
2. **You're on a 2G network** — 2G isn't suitable for MMS, which needs at least 3G.

Let's start with the data. Could you turn mobile data on, then check the network settings and set your network mode to include 4G/5G (for example "4g_5g_preferred")? Let me know what you see after that.
USER: Could you please give me one step at a time? I can only do one action at a time. Let's start with turning mobile data on — should I go ahead with that?
AGENT: Yes, please go ahead and turn mobile data on. Let me know once that's done and what the status bar shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Mobile data is now on. The status bar shows poor signal, still on 2G, and data is enabled now. Battery at 80%.
AGENT: Good. Now let's fix the network mode. Please set your network mode preference to something that includes 4G or 5G — for example "4g_5g_preferred". Let me know once that's done and what the status bar shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Done! Now the status bar shows excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled. Battery still 80%. That looks much better.
AGENT: Excellent — signal, 5G, and data all look good now.

Next, let's check your APN settings, since an incorrect MMSC URL is a common cause of MMS issues. Could you check your APN settings and tell me what the MMSC URL shows?
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
USER: I checked the APN settings. The APN name is "internet", but the MMSC URL shows "Not Set". That could be the problem, right?
AGENT: Yes, that's very likely the problem — without the MMSC URL set, MMS can't be sent or received.

Please reset your APN settings, then reboot your device for the changes to apply. Let me know once that's done.
USER: Could you please give me one step at a time? Should I start by resetting the APN settings?
AGENT: Yes, please start by resetting your APN settings. Let me know once that's done.
TOOL_RESULT: APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, the APN settings are set to reset at reboot. Should I go ahead and reboot the device now?
AGENT: Yes, please go ahead and reboot your device now. Let me know once it's back on.
TOOL_RESULT: Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: My phone has rebooted and is back on. The status bar shows excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled. What should I do next?
AGENT: Good. Now please try sending an MMS again and let me know whether it works.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Hmm, it still won't send. I'm getting a bit frustrated here — I've done everything and it's still not working. What else could be causing this?
AGENT: I understand the frustration — we're close. Let me check a couple more things that commonly interfere with MMS.

First, could you check your Wi-Fi Calling status? Sometimes Wi-Fi Calling can conflict with MMS. Let me know what it shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
USER: Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned off.
AGENT: Thanks. Wi-Fi Calling isn't the issue then.

Next, let's check the messaging app's permissions. Could you check whether the messaging app has "storage" and "sms" permissions granted? Let me know what you find.
TOOL_RESULT: The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
TOOL_RESULT: App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.
USER: I checked the messaging app's permissions. It only has the "phone" permission — it doesn't have "storage" or "sms" permissions granted. That might be the issue.
AGENT: That's likely it — the messaging app needs both storage and SMS permissions to handle media and send MMS.

Please grant the "storage" permission to the messaging app first. Let me know once that's done.
TOOL_RESULT: Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Storage permission granted to the messaging app. Should I go ahead and grant the SMS permission now?
AGENT: Yes, please grant the "sms" permission now. Let me know once that's done.
TOOL_RESULT: Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: SMS permission granted to the messaging app. What should I try next?
AGENT: Now please try sending an MMS again and let me know whether it goes through.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Still no luck — it's not going through. I'm getting pretty frustrated now; we've tried a lot of things. What else could be blocking this?
AGENT: I hear you — let's keep going. There's one more common prerequisite I want to confirm: that basic mobile data actually works for other apps.

Could you open a web browser (with Wi-Fi off, using mobile data) and let me know if you can load a webpage? This tells us whether data connectivity is working end to end.
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi is turned OFF.
TOOL_RESULT: Speed test failed: No Connection.
USER: Wi-Fi is off, and I tried to test my connection but it failed — it says "No Connection." So even though the status bar shows data enabled and 5G, mobile data doesn't actually seem to be working for other apps either.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_data_usage", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1001"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1001", "data_used_gb": "3.2", "data_limit_gb": "5.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_data_usage", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1002", "data_used_gb": "15.1", "data_limit_gb": "15.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_data_usage", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1003"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1003", "data_used_gb": "0.0", "data_limit_gb": "5.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}
AGENT: Found it. Let me confirm which line is yours.

Your phone number 555-123-2002 — could you tell me which line it corresponds to? Actually, let me check: the line tied to your number, **L1002**, has used **15.1 GB of its 15 GB limit** — you've exceeded your plan's data limit, which is why mobile data (and therefore MMS) isn't working even though it shows enabled.

To restore data, I can refuel data for that line. The maximum I can add is 2 GB. Would you like me to do that? If so, how much data would you like to refuel — 1 GB or 2 GB?
USER: Ah, that explains it! Yes, please refuel the full 2 GB for my line.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1002", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1002", "device_id": "D1002", "data_used_gb": 15.1, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": true, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-12-15", "last_sim_replacement_date": "2025-01-20", "suspension_start_date": null}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "P1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"plan_id": "P1002", "name": "Premium Plan", "data_limit_gb": 15.0, "price_per_month": 65.0, "data_refueling_price_per_gb": 2.0}
AGENT: Your plan's refueling rate is **$2 per GB**, so 2 GB will be **$4.00**, added to your bill.

Shall I go ahead and refuel the 2 GB?
USER: Yes, that's fine. Please go ahead and add the 2 GB.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "refuel_data", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1002", "gb_amount": 2}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}
AGENT: Done — I've added 2 GB to your line for $4.00. That brings your data to 17 GB against your 15 GB limit, which should restore connectivity.

Please try loading a webpage again (Wi-Fi off) and then try sending an MMS. Let me know how it goes.
TOOL_RESULT: Speed test failed: No Connection.
USER: Hmm, still no connection — the speed test failed again with "No Connection." The data refuel doesn't seem to have taken effect yet. What should I do?
AGENT: Thanks for testing. A quick thing to try: please reboot your device so the new data allowance takes effect, then test the connection again. Let me know what happens.
TOOL_RESULT: Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
TOOL_RESULT: Speed test failed: No Connection.
USER: I rebooted, and the status bar still shows excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled. But the speed test still fails with "No Connection." It's still not working.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_data_usage", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1002", "data_used_gb": "15.1", "data_limit_gb": "15.0", "data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "D1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"device_id": "D1002", "device_type": "phone", "model": "Smartphone Pro Max", "imei": "234567890123456", "is_esim_capable": true, "activated": true, "activation_date": "2025-02-15 11:45:00", "last_esim_transfer_date": "2025-01-20 09:30:00"}
AGENT: Your device is active and registered normally, and the line is Active with the refuel applied. Everything on the network side looks correct.

Let me have you re-verify two settings one more time, since a failed APN save is a common cause here:

First — please check your APN settings and tell me what the MMSC URL shows now.
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
USER: I checked the APN settings again. Now the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL shows "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc". So that looks correct now.
AGENT: The MMSC URL is set correctly now. Let me check one more setting that can block data — could you check your network status screen and tell me if VPN is connected, or if Data Saver is enabled?

Actually, let's do one at a time. Please check whether **Data Saver** is turned on. Let me know what it shows.
TOOL_RESULT: Data Saver mode is OFF.
USER: Data Saver mode is off.
AGENT: Thanks. Now please check whether **VPN** is connected — sometimes a VPN can block mobile data. Let me know what your status bar shows.
TOOL_RESULT: VPN is turned OFF.
USER: VPN is turned off too. So neither Data Saver nor VPN is the issue.
AGENT: Thanks for checking. Let me be thorough about the network side. Could you check your network status screen and tell me the full details — specifically the network type, signal strength, and whether it shows "registered" or "connected" to the network?
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: Here's what I see:

- Airplane Mode: OFF
- SIM Card Status: active
- Cellular Connection: connected
- Cellular Signal: excellent
- Cellular Network Type: 5G
- Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
- **Data Roaming Enabled: No**
- Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
- Wi-Fi Connected: No

I notice data roaming is turned off — and I'm actually abroad in France right now, so could that be the problem?
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "enable_roaming", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: Roaming was already enabled
AGENT: Roaming is already enabled on your line, so the issue is that roaming needs to be turned on **on your device**.

Please go into your phone's cellular settings and turn **Data Roaming ON** on the device. Then let me know once that's done.
TOOL_RESULT: Data Roaming is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Data Roaming is now turned on. The status bar still shows excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled. Should I try sending an MMS again?
AGENT: Yes, please try sending an MMS again — and also test loading a webpage. Let me know how it goes.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app can send MMS messages.
TOOL_RESULT: Speed Test Result: 275.00 Mbps (Excellent). Connection is very fast.
USER: It's working now! The messaging app says it can send MMS messages, and the speed test shows 275 Mbps — an excellent connection. Turning on data roaming was the fix. Thank you so much for your patience and help!
AGENT: Great news — glad it's all working now! To recap what fixed it: your line was over its data limit (refueled 2 GB for $4.00), the APN/MMSC settings and messaging app permissions needed correcting, and the final piece was enabling data roaming on your device since you're in France.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
USER: No, that's everything I needed. Thanks again for your help — have a great day!

###STOP###

Title: task_[mms_issue]airplane_mode_on|bad_network_preference|break_apn_mms_setting|data_usage_exceeded[PERSONA:Hard].txt
Treat this content as one complete trajectory/workflow context.
Trajectory content:
AGENT: Hi! How can I help you today?
USER: Oh hello. I'm having some trouble with my phone and I'm not very good with these things. I've been trying to send pictures to my daughter - you know, photos of my grandkids - and they just won't go through. It's been like this for a few hours now. Can you help me?
AGENT: I can help with that. First I need to identify you — could you please give me your phone number?
USER: Oh yes, of course. My phone number is 555-123-2002.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_customer_by_phone", "arguments": {"phone_number": "555-123-2002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1001"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1002", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1002", "device_id": "D1002", "data_used_gb": 15.1, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": true, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-12-15", "last_sim_replacement_date": "2025-01-20", "suspension_start_date": null}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "L1003"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1003", "phone_number": "555-123-2003", "status": "Suspended", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1003", "data_used_gb": 0.0, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-06-30", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-10-05", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": "2025-02-01"}
AGENT: Thanks — I've got your line (555-123-2002). Now let's troubleshoot the picture messages.

A couple of quick checks on your phone, please:

1. On your phone, can you check your **status bar**? I need to see what icons are showing — specifically whether you have signal bars, whether mobile data is on, and whether Wi-Fi is connected.
2. Also, please check whether you can **send a regular text message** (not a picture) and whether **mobile data works for other apps** like browsing the web.

Can you tell me what you see?
TOOL_RESULT: Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
USER: Let me take a look at the top of my screen here...

Oh dear, I see a little airplane symbol up there. And the battery shows 80%. Is the airplane a problem?

Should I do those other things you mentioned one at a time? I don't want to get confused doing too much at once.
AGENT: Yes — that little airplane symbol is the problem. When **Airplane Mode** is on, your phone turns off all cellular service and mobile data, so picture messages (and calls and texts) can't go through.

Let's fix just that one thing first:

Please go into your phone's settings and **turn off Airplane Mode** (on most phones you can also swipe down from the top of the screen and tap the airplane icon). Then wait a few seconds and tell me what you see at the top of your screen.
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I turned the airplane off. Let me look at the top of my screen again...

Now I see some signal bars, and it says "2G"? And there's a little "data enabled" thing. The battery is still 80%. Did that fix it?
AGENT: Good progress — Airplane Mode is off, so you have signal and data back. But there's one more issue: **2G** is too slow for picture messages. MMS needs at least a 3G/4G/5G connection.

Please change your network mode:

1. Go into **Settings → Mobile Network / Connections → Network Mode** (the exact wording varies by phone).
2. Change the preferred network mode to **"4G/5G preferred"** or **"4G only"** (any option that includes 3G/4G/5G).

Once you've done that, tell me what network type shows at the top of your screen.
TOOL_RESULT: Network Mode Preference: 2g_only
USER: I found the setting. It was set to "2G only" - I'll change it now.
TOOL_RESULT: Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I changed it. Now the top of my screen shows really good signal bars and it says "5G". That looks much better! Should I try sending my picture now?
AGENT: Yes, please try sending one of your pictures now and let me know if it goes through.

If it still doesn't work, don't worry — there are a couple more things we can check.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Oh bother... I just tried, and it still won't send. The picture just sits there with that little spinning circle. I don't understand - the signal looks great now. This is getting a bit frustrating. What else could be wrong?
AGENT: I understand the frustration — we're close. Let's check a couple more settings. Two quick things, one at a time:

**First, please check your APN settings:**
1. Go to **Settings → Mobile Network → Access Point Names (APN)**.
2. Look for the field labeled **MMSC** (the multimedia message server URL). Tell me whether it has an address filled in, or whether it's blank/not set.

Go ahead and take a look, then tell me what you see.
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
USER: Alright, I found the APN page. It shows the APN name as "internet", but the MMSC line - that's the one you mentioned - it says "Not Set". There's no address in there at all. Is that the problem?
AGENT: Yes — that's the problem. Without an MMSC address, your phone can't send picture messages.

Let's fix it:

1. On that APN screen, look for an option to **reset APN settings** (often in a menu, sometimes labeled "Reset to default").
2. Go ahead and **reset the APN settings**.

After you reset, you'll need to **restart (reboot) your phone** for the change to take effect.

Do the reset first, then reboot, and let me know when you're back up.
TOOL_RESULT: APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I did the reset. It says the APN settings will reset when I restart the phone.

But wait - you want me to restart it? I'm a little nervous about that. Will I lose all my photos of the grandkids if I restart? That's the one thing I really don't want to happen.
AGENT: No, don't worry — restarting your phone is completely safe. It's just turning it off and back on. **All your photos, contacts, and settings stay exactly where they are.** Nothing gets erased.

Go ahead and restart it whenever you're ready, then let me know when it's back on.
TOOL_RESULT: Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, it's back on now. The screen shows my normal stuff again, and the top still shows great signal with "5G". Everything looks fine. Should I try sending the picture again?
AGENT: Yes, please give it a try now and let me know if the picture goes through.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Oh no... I tried again and it still won't send! The little circle keeps spinning and then it just stops. I really don't understand what's going on. We've done so many things now. 

Is there anything else that could be causing this?
AGENT: I hear you — we've done a lot. Let's check two last things, one at a time.

**First, let's check your Wi-Fi Calling setting:**
1. Go to **Settings → Connections / Mobile Network → Wi-Fi Calling**.
2. Tell me whether Wi-Fi Calling is **On** or **Off**.

Take a look and let me know.
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
USER: I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is turned **Off** on my phone. Should it be on?
AGENT: No, Off is fine — that's not the issue. Good, one less thing.

**Last thing to check — the messaging app's permissions:**
1. Go to **Settings → Apps → Messages (your messaging app) → Permissions**.
2. I need to know whether **Storage** and **SMS** permissions are listed as **allowed/granted**.

Tell me what you see for those two.
TOOL_RESULT: The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
TOOL_RESULT: App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, storage, phone.
USER: Let me look... Okay, I found the Messages app permissions. It shows **SMS** and **Storage** both listed, and they seem to be allowed. There's also "phone" in there. So those look okay to me.

So what now? We've tried so many things and it's still not working. I'm starting to worry I'll never get these pictures to my daughter.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_data_usage", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"line_id": "L1002", "data_used_gb": "15.1", "data_limit_gb": "15.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_details_by_id", "arguments": {"id": "P1002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"plan_id": "P1002", "name": "Premium Plan", "data_limit_gb": 15.0, "price_per_month": 65.0, "data_refueling_price_per_gb": 2.0}
AGENT: I found it. Your line has used **15.1 GB** of data this billing cycle, but your plan's limit is **15 GB** — so you've gone over, and that's why your data (and picture messages) stopped working.

The fix is to add more data ("refuel") to your line. Here's how it works:
- We can add up to **2 GB**.
- The price is **$2 per GB**.

How many GB would you like to add? (For example, 1 GB would be $2, 2 GB would be $4.)
USER: Ah, that would explain it! I've been up to the limit.

Well, I don't want to change my plan or anything fancy - but I'll happily add the data. Let's go with the full **2 GB** please. That should get me through the rest of the month, and $4 sounds reasonable.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "refuel_data", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1002", "gb_amount": 2}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}
AGENT: Done! I've added **2 GB** of data to your line for **$4**, which will be added to your bill. Your line now has enough data to get through the rest of the month.

Please try sending your picture again now — it should go through. Let me know!
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app can send MMS messages.
USER: Oh wonderful! It worked! The picture just went through - I can see it sent! 

Thank you so much for your patience with me. I know I got a bit flustered there, but you walked me through it and now the grandkids' photos are headed to my daughter. I really appreciate your help!
AGENT: You're very welcome — I'm so glad the photos made it through to your daughter! It was a few things stacked up (Airplane Mode, the 2G network, the missing MMSC address, plus going over your data limit), but we got there.

Enjoy sharing those grandkid photos. If anything else comes up, just reach out. Take care!
USER: Thank you so much, you've been very kind. I'll remember to keep an eye on that data from now on! Have a wonderful day.

###STOP###

Title: task_[mms_issue]bad_network_preference|bad_wifi_calling|break_app_sms_permission|data_mode_off|unseat_sim_card|user_abroad_roaming_enabled_off[PERSONA:Hard].txt
Treat this content as one complete trajectory/workflow context.
Trajectory content:
AGENT: Hi! How can I help you today?
USER: Hi, um, I hope you can help me. I've been trying to send picture messages to my family, and they just won't go through. It's been like this for a few hours now and I'm getting a bit worried. Could you help me figure out what's wrong?
AGENT: I can help you with that. First, I need to verify your identity.

Could you please provide your **phone number**? (Or alternatively, your customer ID, or your full name and date of birth.)
USER: Oh, of course. My phone number is 555-123-2002. My name is John Smith, if that helps too.
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "get_customer_by_phone", "arguments": {"phone_number": "555-123-2002"}}
TOOL_RESULT: {"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}
AGENT: Thanks, John — I've verified your account.

Now let's troubleshoot your picture messaging (MMS). To narrow down the cause, could you run a couple of checks on your phone?

1. **Can you make calls and use mobile data** (e.g., browse the web) normally?
2. Please run **`check_network_status`** on your device and tell me what it shows.

Also, let me know which phone number/line you're trying to send the pictures from (you have a few lines on your account).
USER: Let me run that check for you.
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: Okay, I ran that check. Honestly, a lot of it doesn't look good. It says:
- Airplane mode is OFF
- SIM Card Status: **missing**
- Cellular Connection: no service
- Mobile Data Enabled: No
- Data Roaming Enabled: No
- Wi-Fi is OFF and not connected

That "missing SIM card" part doesn't sound good at all! And to answer your other question, I'm trying to send the pictures from this same line — 555-123-2002. Does that missing SIM explain why nothing works?
AGENT: Yes, that's very likely the root cause. If your phone reports the SIM card as **missing**, the phone can't connect to the cellular network at all — which means no calls, no mobile data, and no picture messages. Everything else depends on that first.

Let's get the SIM seated properly. On your device, please run:

**`reseat_sim_card()`**

That will reseat the SIM so it makes proper contact. Once you've done that, run **`check_network_status`** again and tell me what it shows — we want to see signal strength and mobile data come back.
USER: Alright, let me try that.
TOOL_RESULT: SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, I reseated the SIM card. Let me run that network check again.
TOOL_RESULT: Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: poor
Cellular Network Type: 2G
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
USER: Okay, that's a bit better! Now it says:
- SIM Card Status: **active** ✓
- Cellular Connection: connected
- Cellular Signal: **poor**
- Cellular Network Type: **2G**
- Mobile Data Enabled: **No**
- Data Roaming Enabled: **No**
- Wi-Fi is still OFF

So the SIM is being recognized now, which is good. But the mobile data is still turned off, and I notice data roaming is off too. Since I'm currently in France (I'm traveling), could that be part of the problem?
AGENT_TOOL_CALL: {"name": "enable_roaming", "arguments": {"customer_id": "C1001", "line_id": "L1001"}}
TOOL_RESULT: Roaming enabled successfully
AGENT: Done — data roaming is now **enabled** on your line at no cost. ✓

Summary of what to do on your end:

1. **Set network mode to 4G/5G** — run `set_network_mode_preference(mode: "4g_5g_preferred")` (2G isn't suitable for MMS).
2. **Turn mobile data ON.**

Once you've done both, please run **`check_status_bar`** (or `check_network_status`) and tell me what it shows. Then we'll test the MMS again.
USER: Oh dear, that's two things at once and I want to make sure I don't mess anything up. Could you walk me through them one at a time, please? Which should I do first?
AGENT: No problem — let's do one at a time.

**Step 1:** Please run this on your device now:

**`set_network_mode_preference(mode: "4g_5g_preferred")`**

This switches you off 2G onto a network that supports picture messaging.

Once you've done that, tell me what the result says, and I'll give you the next step.
USER: Alright, let me do that first step.
TOOL_RESULT: Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
USER: That worked! It says the Preferred Network Mode is now set to 4g_5g_preferred. And the status bar is looking much better — I've got excellent signal and it shows 5G now. Though it still says "Data Disabled."

What's the next step?
AGENT: Excellent — 4G/5G preferred is set, and you've got excellent signal on 5G now. 🎉

**Step 2:** Now please turn **mobile data ON** on your device (it currently shows "Data Disabled").

Once you've done that, tell me what the status bar shows, and we'll verify everything is good for sending picture messages.
USER: Okay, turning on mobile data now.
TOOL_RESULT: Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Done! Mobile data is now ON. The status bar shows:
- Signal: **Excellent**
- **5G**
- **Data Enabled** ✓
- Battery: 80%

That looks much better than before! Should I try sending a picture message now?
AGENT: Yes, please go ahead and try sending a picture message now — that's the perfect test.

If it goes through, let me know and we're all set. If it still fails, tell me and we'll check a couple more things (the APN/MMSC settings and the messaging app permissions).
USER: Let me try sending a picture message now.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Hmm, no luck — it still won't send the picture message. That's a little frustrating after all those steps. What else can we try?
AGENT: No worries — we're close. Let's check the APN settings, since a missing MMSC (the server that handles picture messages) is a very common cause.

Please run this and tell me the result:

**`check_apn_settings()`**
TOOL_RESULT: Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
USER: Okay, I ran that check. It shows:
- APN Name: **internet**
- MMSC URL: **http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc**

So both of those seem to be filled in. Does that look right to you? What's next?
AGENT: Yes, that looks correct — the APN name and MMSC URL are both set properly, so that's not the issue.

Next, let's check Wi-Fi Calling, since it can sometimes interfere with picture messaging. Please run this and tell me the result:

**`check_wifi_calling_status()`**
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
USER: Okay, it says Wi-Fi Calling is currently **turned ON**. Could that be causing the problem? What should I do?
AGENT: That could indeed be interfering with your picture messages. Please turn Wi-Fi Calling **OFF** by running:

**`toggle_wifi_calling()`**

Once you've done that, try sending a picture message again and let me know how it goes.
TOOL_RESULT: Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF. Let me try sending that picture message again.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Still no good — it says my messaging app still can't send the picture message. We've tried quite a few things now, and I'm starting to worry we won't get this sorted. What else can we check?
AGENT: We still have a couple of things to check — don't worry, we'll get there.

Next, let's verify the messaging app has the permissions it needs. Please run this and tell me the result:

**`check_app_permissions(app_name="messaging")`**
TOOL_RESULT: App 'messaging' has permission for: storage, phone.
USER: Okay, I ran that. It says the messaging app has permission for: **storage** and **phone**. That's it. Is it missing something it needs?
AGENT: Yes — it's missing the **SMS** permission, which the messaging app needs to send messages. Let's grant it.

Please run this:

**`grant_app_permission(app_name="messaging", permission="sms")`**

Once done, try sending the picture message again and let me know what happens.
TOOL_RESULT: Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
USER: Okay, the SMS permission was granted. Let me try that picture message one more time.
TOOL_RESULT: Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
USER: Oh, this is getting really frustrating. It *still* won't send — same message as before. We've done so many things now. Is there anything else left to try? I really need to get these photos to my grandchildren.
AGENT: I hear you — let's keep at it. Let me re-verify all the prerequisites at once so we can catch anything we missed.

Please run these two checks and tell me both results:

1. **`check_network_status()`**
2. **`check_apn_settings()`**
USER: Oh, two things at once again — I'm sorry, I get a bit flustered with doing several things together. Could you give me just one at a time? Which check should I run first?
AGENT: Of course — one at a time.
